brief: Goldman's weekly cross-asset positioning note (Pierre Saboureault, Sales/Trading, not research) reports hedge fund deleveraging accelerating: beta-adjusted fundamental long/short gross leverage fell to a one-year low (214.2%) and net leverage to a five-year low (48.2%), driven by the largest shorting week since April 2025, with single stocks net sold for a 10th straight week and macro products net bought for a 5th. CTAs have shed length and are now short the S&P 500 and Nasdaq, and a VIX spike above 35 plus the 4th-largest option volume session ever pushed the desk's Vol Panic Index to 9.8/10. Against this, US equity mutual funds and ETFs took in near $170bn since Q4 began, buybacks ran at 2.2x pace, and overall PB gross leverage still sits at the 89th percentile. The note concludes positioning cleanup is uneven, consensus is thin, and the next catalyst is unclear: it frames whether 2026 mirrors 2018, and whether a Fed pivot to tightening financial conditions would be the inflexion trigger.
